body:
Summary

A Codex solver can be blocked before implementation when a task requires a specific Codex plugin or Agent Skills workflow and that capability is not already available in the solver session.

The solver attempted to install the required official plugin, but the environment-provided plugin installation workflow rejected it because the plugin was not present in the recommended_plugins allowlist. There was no supported fallback available to the solver, so it correctly stopped without touching the repository.

This was observed while solving CEHR2005/GCS-TS#1, which intentionally requires the official Superpowers workflow before any implementation.

Actual behavior

The Codex solver returned:

> Blocked by the mandatory Superpowers preflight; no implementation work was started.

Attempted steps:

Inspected the session-provided installed skills/plugins. No superpowers:* skill or superpowers@openai-curated-remote plugin capability is available.

Called the environment plugin-install workflow with the exact ID superpowers@openai-curated-remote.

The install request failed with the exact error: plugin_id must match one of the entries in the <recommended_plugins> list.

Because installation failed, superpowers:using-superpowers could not be invoked. The other mandated Superpowers workflows likewise cannot be invoked.

Per the issue hard preflight and stop conditions, I did not inspect implementation details or modify repository files. The temporary local files used to read issue/PR metadata were removed, and the worktree remains clean.

Human action needed: make the official superpowers@openai-curated-remote plugin available in this environment, then rerun the solver.



This is a correct fail-closed response from the model, but it leaves the Hive Mind operator without a task-level way to satisfy the prerequisite.

Expected behavior

Hive Mind should provide a supported and reproducible way for an operator to make required Codex plugins or Agent Skills available before codex exec starts.

At minimum, Hive Mind should:

1. Document how an operator can preinstall a Codex plugin into the persistent /home/box/.codex state.


2. Verify that the plugin or skills remain visible inside --isolation docker solver containers.


3. Fail early with an operator-actionable diagnostic when a configured required capability is unavailable.



Ideally, Hive Mind would provide a generic configuration mechanism for required Codex plugins or Agent Skills rather than a Superpowers-specific special case.

Relevant Hive Mind context

src/codex.lib.mjs launches codex exec and inherits the process environment.

src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs mounts the parent ~/.codex into /home/box/.codex for Docker-isolated Codex tasks.

The documented Docker deployment persists /home/box/.codex, so an operator-installed marketplace plugin should be able to propagate to new solver sessions.

Hive Mind already has a project-local skill deployment precedent in src/handoff-skill.lib.mjs, which installs and git-excludes the HANDOFF skill before the AI tool starts.

The recommended_plugins restriction does not appear to be implemented by Hive Mind itself. It appears to come from the Codex session/plugin-install environment. However, Hive Mind still needs an operator-facing integration path because the solver cannot resolve the condition itself.


Reproduction

1. Run a Hive Mind task using --tool codex, including Docker isolation if applicable.


2. Use an issue that explicitly requires superpowers:using-superpowers and instructs the solver to install superpowers@openai-curated-remote if it is absent.


3. Start with a persistent ~/.codex that does not already contain Superpowers.


4. Observe that the session exposes no superpowers:* skills.


5. Observe that the installation attempt fails with:

plugin_id must match one of the entries in the <recommended_plugins> list


6. The solver stops before implementation.



Possible solutions

Any of the following could provide a clean resolution:

Document and validate an operator preinstallation flow using Codex's interactive /plugins UI inside the parent Hive Mind container.

Add startup configuration for required Codex plugins and verify them before accepting tasks.

Add a generic project-local Agent Skills deployment mechanism modeled on deployHandoffSkill.

Propagate a persistent ~/.agents/skills directory into Docker-isolated Codex tasks.

Provide a supported initialization hook that can install a pinned official Agent Skills repository before codex exec.


For Superpowers specifically, subagent workflows also require Codex multi-agent support to be enabled, for example:

[features]
multi_agent = true

The selected solution should make the effective child-session configuration verifiable.

Acceptance criteria

[ ] An operator can declare or provision a required Codex plugin or Agent Skill for Hive Mind solver sessions.

[ ] The capability is available in both direct and --isolation docker Codex runs.

[ ] Installation and configuration persist across documented Hive Mind container restarts.

[ ] A preflight reports the exact missing capability and an actionable remediation command or path.

[ ] The solution does not modify the target repository or commit deployed skill files.

[ ] Tests cover direct execution, Docker isolation propagation, missing capability, and successful capability discovery.

[ ] Documentation explains the interaction between persistent /home/box/.codex, optional ~/.agents/skills, and image-provided configuration.


Additional context

The official Superpowers repository documents a native Codex installation using an Agent Skills symlink:

https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/.codex/INSTALL.md

Applying that command only inside the parent Hive Mind container might not be sufficient for Docker-isolated tasks unless the corresponding .agents path is also propagated or the skills are deployed into the task workspace.

Original blocked task:

https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/issues/1

comments.body:
We need to make sure we auto detect all required plugins, skills and so on, and preinstall all dependencies in solve command before starting codex/claude command, so everything needed for AI harnesses is already prepared and available, so they can continue working as expected.

We also need to make sure these changes are applied not globally for all tasks, but per repository locally, so other tasks will be executed as expected also.

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

title: Codex solver cannot provision required plugins outside recommended_plugins allowlist
